mainTopic: Whether כהנים are 'our agents' or 'agents of Heaven', tested through a מודר הנאה, and רבי יוחנן's rule that the offerings of מחוסרי כפרה need no consent.
overview: The משנה lists more things a person may do for someone who is forbidden by נדר to benefit from him. He may separate his תרומה and מעשרות, offer certain קרבנות for him, and teach him מדרש, הלכות and אגדות, but not מקרא. The גמרא asks whether כהנים act as our agents (שלוחי דידן) or as agents of Heaven (שלוחי דשמיא), which matters for a מודר הנאה. It tries to prove from the משנה that they are Heaven's agents. It rejects the proof: the משנה lists only offerings of מחוסרי כפרה, and as רבי יוחנן teaches, those need no consent, since a father brings them even for his young children ('זאת תורת הזב'). The גמרא then challenges רבי יוחנן: does 'זאת תורת היולדת' include a young girl, who cannot safely give birth? It answers that this פסוק includes a שוטה, whose husband brings her קרבן. That matches רבי יהודה, who says a husband brings all his wife's קרבנות because of what he promised in her כתובה.

steps.title: משנה: Separating tithes and offering sacrifices for the forbidden person
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits the person to separate תרומה and מעשרות for the מודר הנאה with the owner's consent. He may also offer the bird-pairs of זבין, זבות and יולדות, and חטאות and אשמות, for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: And he may separate his תרומה and מעשרות with his consent. He may also offer for him the bird-pairs of זבין, זבות and יולדות, and חטאות and אשמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of things one may do for a person who is forbidden by נדר to benefit from him. Here it covers separating tithes and offering certain קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is someone forbidden to get benefit from this man. The משנה still allows the man to separate תרומה for him with the owner's consent. If he is a כהן, he may also offer specific קרבנות for him. The exact list of offerings will become important in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Separates תרומה (the כהן's portion) from produce
With his (the owner's) knowledge and consent
Bird-pairs (two doves or pigeons) brought as offerings
Men or women who had a ritually impure discharge
Women who gave birth

phrases.english: MISHNA:
And he separates his terumah and his tithes with his consent,
phrases.notes: 'His' means the produce of the person who is forbidden to benefit. He has to agree to it.

phrases.english: and he offers for him the bird-pairs of zavin,
the bird-pairs of zavot, the bird-pairs of women after childbirth,
sin-offerings and guilt-offerings.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: He may separate תרומה and מעשרות for the מודר הנאה with the owner's consent. He may offer for him the קינים of זבין, זבות and יולדות, and חטאות and אשמות.

steps.title: משנה: What he may and may not teach him
steps.stepSummary: He may teach the מודר הנאה מדרש, הלכות and אגדות, but not מקרא. He may, however, teach the man's children מקרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he may teach him מדרש, הלכות and אגדות, but not מקרא. But he may teach his sons and daughters מקרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list. It tells us which kinds of Torah learning he may teach the forbidden person, and which he may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching מדרש, הלכות and אגדות is allowed. Teaching מקרא to the person himself is not. His children are treated differently: they may be taught מקרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Explanations derived from the פסוקים
Laws
Non-legal Torah teachings and stories
Scripture, the written text of תנ״ך

phrases.english: And he teaches him midrash, halachos, and aggados,
but he may not teach him Scripture.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְלַמֵּד הוּא אֶת בָּנָיו וְאֶת בְּנוֹתָיו מִקְרָא.
phrases.english: However, he may teach his sons and his daughters Scripture.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching מדרש, הלכות and אגדות is permitted. Teaching מקרא to him is forbidden. Teaching מקרא to his children is permitted.

steps.title: Are כהנים our agents or Heaven's agents?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether כהנים act as our agents or as agents of Heaven. The difference shows up with a מודר הנאה: if they are our agents, offering his קרבן is a forbidden benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They asked: Are these כהנים our agents or agents of Heaven? What difference does it make? It matters for someone forbidden by נדר to benefit. If they are our agents, the כהן is benefiting him, and it is forbidden. If they are agents of Heaven, it is permitted. Which is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a basic question about what a כהן is when he serves in the בית המקדש. It then explains why the answer matters in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose a כהן is the owner's agent (שלוחי דידן). Then bringing the קרבן is a favor done for the owner, so a מודר הנאה may not accept it. Suppose instead the כהן is Heaven's agent (שלוחי דשמיא). Then he is serving ה׳, not doing the owner a favor, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
Our agents
Agents of Heaven
Practical difference
Someone forbidden by נדר to benefit from another

steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether כהנים are שלוחי דידן or שלוחי דשמיא is a well-known foundational question that comes up in many places.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
A question was raised before them:
These kohanim, are they our agents,
or agents of Heaven?
What is the practical difference?
For one forbidden by vow from benefit.
If you say that they are our agents,
then he is giving him benefit, and it is forbidden.
And if you say agents of Heaven, it is permitted.
What is it?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether כהנים serve as the owners' agents or as agents of Heaven, which decides whether a מודר הנאה may have them offer his קרבן.

steps.title: Attempted proof from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from our משנה that כהנים are agents of Heaven. The משנה lets the person offer קרבנות for the מודר הנאה, and that would be a forbidden benefit if they were our agents.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear, as we learned: He offers for him the bird-pairs of זבין, etc. If you say they are our agents, he would be giving him benefit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה from Step 1 as proof. Since the משנה allows a כהן to offer the forbidden person's קרבנות, it seems כהנים must be Heaven's agents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning works from the end result back to its cause. The משנה permits it. If כהנים were our agents, it would be forbidden. So the משנה must hold that כהנים are agents of Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof)
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: Come and hear, as we learned:
He offers for him the bird-pairs of zavin, etc.
phrases.notes: This is quoting our own משנה, from Step 1.

phrases.english: If you say they are our agents,
isn't he giving him benefit?

steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה permitting him to offer the קינים of זבין and other offerings for the מודר הנאה

steps.title: Why does the משנה list only specific offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. If כהנים were simply Heaven's agents, the משנה should have said 'he offers his קרבנות' in general, not just these specific ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, let it teach: he offers for him sacrifices!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from Step 4. It points out that the משנה gave a narrow list instead of a general rule. This sets up the real explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being Heaven's agents were the reason, any קרבן at all would be allowed. The משנה would then just say 'קרבנות.' The choice of a specific list shows that something special about these offerings is the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning
Let it teach (the משנה should have said)

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
let it teach: he offers for him sacrifices!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה that כהנים are שלוחי דשמיא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה gives a limited list instead of permitting all קרבנות. So its reason cannot be a general rule about כהנים.

steps.title: Offerings of those lacking atonement are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the משנה another way. The offerings of מחוסרי כפרה are special, because, as רבי יוחנן teaches, they do not need the owner's consent. He learns this from the fact that a father brings such offerings for his young children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, those lacking atonement are different. As רבי יוחנן said: Everyone requires consent, except for those lacking atonement. For a person brings an offering for his minor sons and daughters, as it says: 'This is the law of the זב,' whether adult or minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes rejecting the proof by giving a different reason for the משנה. Its rule comes from the special status of מחוסרי כפרה, not from כהנים being Heaven's agents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a קרבן needs its owner's דעת. The offerings of מחוסרי כפרה can be brought even without it. The proof is that a father brings them for his young children, who have no legal דעת. So the משנה can permit these offerings even if כהנים are שלוחי דידן, and the question stays unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: People who still need an offering to finish their purification
Is different
Need (the owner's) knowledge and consent
Minors, young children

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's permission covers only the offerings of מחוסרי כפרה, which need no consent. So it does not prove whether כהנים are שלוחי דידן or שלוחי דשמיא.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא decided that כהנים are our agents. It only showed that the משנה's list can be explained without deciding either way.

phrases.english: Rather, those lacking atonement are different.
As Rabbi Yochanan said:
Everyone requires consent,
except for those lacking atonement.
For a person brings an offering
for his minor sons and daughters,
as it is stated: "This is the law of the zav,"
whether an adult or a minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection begun in Step 5 by giving the real reason for the משנה's specific list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the source: the משנה's ruling rests on a special rule for מחוסרי כפרה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה permits offering קרבנות because כהנים are שלוחי דשמיא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה permits only offerings of מחוסרי כפרה, which need no owner's consent, so no proof can be drawn about the status of כהנים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of שלוחי דידן or שלוחי דשמיא is not resolved by this משנה.

steps.title: Does 'the law of a woman after childbirth' include a young girl?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. By his reasoning, 'זאת תורת היולדת' would have to include a קטנה. But a ברייתא shows that a קטנה cannot safely give birth at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But now, according to רבי יוחנן, would 'This is the law of a woman after childbirth' include both a young girl and an adult? Can a young girl even give birth? רב ביבי taught before רב נחמן: three women may use a contraceptive cloth: a young girl, a pregnant woman, and a nursing woman. A young girl, because she might become pregnant and die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's way of reading 'זאת תורת'. It shows that reading this phrase the same way in a different פסוק leads to an impossible result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן learned from the words 'זאת תורת' that a קרבן can be brought for a minor. If the same words appear by a יולדת, they should include a minor girl who gave birth. But a ברייתא says a קטנה is in danger of dying if she becomes pregnant, so a law written for a קטנה יולדת seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so. Opens a challenge that follows from what was just said.
A woman who gave birth. She must bring קרבנות afterward.
A young girl who is not yet an adult in הלכה
A soft cloth used to prevent pregnancy
A nursing mother

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא about the מוך is not the main topic here. It is brought only to prove that a קטנה is not expected to give birth.

phrases.english: But now, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan,
phrases.notes: He means: since רבי יוחנן reads 'זאת תורת' as including minors.

phrases.english: 'This is the law of a woman who gives birth, etc.'
would it apply to both a minor and an adult?
Is a minor capable of giving birth?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא תָּנֵי רַב בִּיבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Beivai teach before Rav Naḥman:
Three women may have relations using a contraceptive cloth:
a minor, a pregnant woman, and a nursing woman.
A minor, because she might become pregnant and die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source רבי יוחנן used in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading of 'זאת תורת' as including minors
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the same words appear by a יולדת, they should include a minor. But a minor is not expected to give birth, as the ברייתא of the מוך shows.

steps.title: The verse includes a woman who is a שוטה, not a minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that by a יולדת, the words 'זאת תורת' include a שוטה. A husband brings the קרבן for his wife even if she is a שוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse, 'This is the law of a woman after childbirth', includes both a competent woman and a שוטה, since a man brings a קרבן for his wife who is a שוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different meaning to the extra words in the יולדת פסוק, so they no longer point to a minor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'זאת תורת' by a יולדת still teach something new. They teach about a שוטה instead of a קטנה. This fits רבי יוחנן's main idea: a קרבן can be brought for someone who cannot give consent.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is mentally competent
A woman who is not mentally competent in הלכה

phrases.english: That verse, 'This is the law of a woman who gives birth,'
teaches both a competent woman and an incompetent woman,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אָדָם מֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן עַל אִשְׁתּוֹ שׁוֹטָה,
phrases.english: since a man brings an offering for his wife who is incompetent.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהִיא ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַיֹּלֶדֶת״, בֵּין פִּקַּחַת בֵּין שׁוֹטָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets what the extra words include
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זאת תורת היולדת' would include a minor, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: It includes a שוטה, whose husband brings her קרבן.

steps.title: Source: רבי יהודה says a husband brings his wife's offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that this answer matches רבי יהודה. In a ברייתא, he rules that a husband brings a rich person's קרבן for his wife, and all the קרבנות she owes.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows the words of רבי יהודה, as it was taught: רבי יהודה says, a man brings a rich person's offering for his wife, and all the offerings she is obligated in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer from step 8 by quoting a ברייתא of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that a husband brings his wife's קרבן is not a new invention. רבי יהודה says the husband pays for all her קרבנות. If he is wealthy, he brings the more expensive קרבן עשיר.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the words of
As it was taught in a ברייתא
The more expensive offering a wealthy person brings

phrases.english: This follows the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
As it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם מֵבִיא קׇרְבַּן עָשִׁיר עַל אִשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: A man brings a wealthy person's offering for his wife,
phrases.notes: A rich יולדת brings a lamb, and a poor one brings birds. The husband's wealth decides which one.

phrases.english: and all the offerings she is obligated to bring,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 8 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband brings his wife's קרבן

steps.title: The reason: the husband takes on her obligations in the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's reason is that in the כתובה, the husband writes that he takes responsibility for the obligations she had from before. Her קרבנות are included, even if she is a שוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For this is what he writes for her: 'And the responsibility that you have, is upon me, from before this time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why the husband must bring his wife's קרבנות: he promised this in the כתובה. This wraps up the answer to the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's duty comes from a money obligation he took on, not from his wife appointing him. So the קרבן can be brought without her consent. This shows again that the קרבנות of מחוסרי כפרה are special, and our משנה does not prove that כהנים are Heaven's agents.

keyTerms.meaning: Responsibility for paying obligations
From before this time

steps.whatToRemember: The קרבנות of מחוסרי כפרה, like a יולדת's, can be brought without the owner's knowledge. A husband brings them even for a wife who is a שוטה. So the משנה allowing such קרבנות for a מודר הנאה fits even if כהנים are our agents.

phrases.english: For this is what he writes for her:
'And the responsibility that you have is upon me,'
'from before this time.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבי יהודה's ruling in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A husband brings his wife's קרבנות because of his כתובה obligation, even without her consent. This supports the view that the קרבנות of מחוסרי כפרה need no consent, so the proof that כהנים are Heaven's agents falls away.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband brings his wife's קרבנות even without her consent, because he took on her obligations
steps.raayaSupportSource: The כתובה clause 'ואחריות דאית ליך עלי מן קדמת דנא' cited in רבי יהודה's ברייתא
